main_point.en: Our lives must elevate Jesus instead of ourselves.

christ_connection.en: John the Baptist said he wasn’t the groom; he was the friend of the groom. As the friend, it was his responsibility to decrease in status and to elevate Jesus. Jesus is the Groom from above who came to give His life for His bride—those who receive His Word and believe in Him.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 施洗約翰說，他不是新郎，而是新郎的朋友。身為新郎的朋友，他有責任降低自己的地位，高舉耶穌。耶穌是從天上而來的新郎，祂來為自己的新婦捨命——就是那些接受祂的話語並相信祂的人。

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We Repent

content.en:
1 In those days John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea, 
2 “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” 
3 For this is he who was spoken of by the prophet Isaiah when he said, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’” 
4 Now John wore a garment of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey. 
5 Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region about the Jordan were going out to him, 
6 and they were baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
content.zh-Hant:
1 那時，有施洗的約翰出來，在猶太的曠野傳道，說：
2 「天國近了，你們應當悔改！」
3 這人就是先知以賽亞所說的。他說：「在曠野有人聲喊著說：預備主的道，修直他的路！」
4 這約翰身穿駱駝毛的衣服，腰束皮帶，吃的是蝗蟲、野蜜。
5 那時，耶路撒冷和猶太全地，並約旦河一帶地方的人，都出去到約翰那裏，
6 承認他們的罪，在約旦河裏受他的洗。

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We’re Authentic

content.en:
7 But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? 
8 Bear fruit in keeping with repentance. 
9 And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father,’ for I tell you, God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. 
10 Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. 
11 I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who is coming after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. 
12 His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”
content.zh-Hant:
7 約翰看見許多法利賽人和撒都該人也來受洗，就對他們說：「毒蛇的種類！誰指示你們逃避將來的忿怒呢？
8 你們要結出果子來，與悔改的心相稱。
9 不要自己心裏說：『有亞伯拉罕為我們的祖宗。』我告訴你們，神能從這些石頭中給亞伯拉罕興起子孫來。
10 現在斧子已經放在樹根上，凡不結好果子的樹就砍下來，丟在火裏。
11 我是用水給你們施洗，叫你們悔改。但那在我以後來的，能力比我更大，我就是給他提鞋也不配。他要用聖靈與火給你們施洗。
12 他手裏拿著簸箕，要揚淨他的場，把麥子收在倉裏，把糠用不滅的火燒盡了。」

content.en: Leaders: May we live in a way that reveals “fruit consistent with repentance” (Matt. 3:8).
content.zh-Hant: 帶領者：願我們活出「結出果子來，與悔改的心相稱」（太 3:8）的生命。

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We Repent

content.en: “John’s lifestyle declares that he lived fully for the will of God, not valuing possessions, comfort or status. Blinded by our society’s values, we too often preach a Christianity that merely ‘meets our needs’ rather than one that calls us to sacrifice our highest desires for the kingdom. Too many Western Christians live a religion that costs nothing, treats the kingdom cheaply and therefore does not demand saving faith. Saving faith includes believing God’s grace so sincerely that we live as if his message is true and stake our lives on it. May we have the courage to trust God as John did, to stake everything on the kingdom (13:46) and to relinquish our own popularity, when necessary, by summoning others to stake everything on the kingdom as well.”¹
content.zh-Hant: 「約翰的生活方式宣告，他完全為神的旨意而活，不看重財物、舒適或地位。我們被社會的價值觀蒙蔽，太常宣講一種只『滿足我們的需要』的基督教信仰，而不是呼召我們為了神的國犧牲最高渴望的信仰。太多西方基督徒活在一種毫無代價、把神的國看得廉價的宗教中，因此不要求使人得救的信心。使人得救的信心包括如此真誠地相信神的恩典，以致我們活得彷彿祂的信息是真實的，並把自己的生命押在這信息上。願我們有勇氣像約翰一樣信靠神，把一切都押在神的國上（13:46）；在必要時，放下自己的聲望，呼召別人也把一切都押在神的國上。」¹

content.en: “In Isaiah, God is pictured as coming to his people, exiled in Babylon, to deliver them and to lead them home. Matthew applies the passage to John and Jesus—John being the voice of one crying in the wilderness whose mission is to prepare the way of the Lord, Jesus being the Lord who is coming to save his people. In biblical perspective, initiative is with God in creation, revelation, and redemption. God creates; God reveals himself; and God comes to man to save him. In many religious systems, man is seen as discovering God and establishing himself before God, whether through ritual, works, goodness, asceticism, knowledge, or otherwise.”²
content.zh-Hant: 「在以賽亞書中，神被描繪為來到那些被擄到巴比倫的子民中，要拯救他們，並帶領他們回家。馬太把這段經文應用在約翰和耶穌身上——約翰是在曠野呼喊者的聲音，他的使命是預備主的道；耶穌就是那位要來拯救祂子民的主。從聖經的角度來看，創造、啟示和救贖的主動權都在神。神創造；神啟示自己；神來到人這裏拯救人。在許多宗教體系中，人被視為可以藉著儀式、行為、善行、苦修、知識或其他方式發現神，並在神面前建立自己的地位。」²

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We’re Authentic

content.en: “John again reminds his listeners that they dare not trust in their ancestral credentials or believe that they alone are legitimate candidates for inclusion in the people of God. Matthew’s two-pronged emphasis, introduced in chaps. 1–2, thus continues: the messianic age brings new people into God’s kingdom and excludes others who thought themselves secure. The Messiah is the true Son of Abraham (1:1-2); apart from him there is no salvation.”³
content.zh-Hant: 「約翰再次提醒聽眾，他們不敢倚靠祖先的身分資歷，也不可相信只有他們才是有資格被納入神子民中的人。馬太在第1至2章引入的雙重重點就此延續：彌賽亞時代把新的人帶進神的國，也排除那些以為自己穩妥的人。彌賽亞是亞伯拉罕真正的兒子（1:1-2）；離了祂就沒有救恩。」³

content.en: “John was indeed a great man (11:11-14), but he derived his greatness from the even greater One whom he served. To illustrate the contrast between himself and the Messiah, John thought of the lowest of all tasks (removal of another person’s sandals), and then said he was even below that. He was voicing the impossibility of comparison between his humanity and the Messiah-King’s deity.”⁴
content.zh-Hant: 「約翰確實是偉大的人（11:11-14），但他的偉大來自他所事奉的那位更偉大者。為了說明自己與彌賽亞之間的對比，約翰想到所有工作中最低微的一項（替另一個人脫鞋），然後說自己甚至不配做這件事。他是在表達，他的人性與彌賽亞君王的神性之間根本無法相比。」⁴

content.en: John the Baptist fulfilled prophecy: He cried out in the wilderness and prepared the way for the Messiah (Isa. 40:3). John was like a king’s herald, who went ahead of the king to smooth the road for easier travel and to announce his upcoming arrival to a town or city. After roughly four hundred years of prophetic silence, John called the people back to God, much like Elijah did in 1 Kings 18. During this period, the Pharisees and Sadducees were like religious political groups; most of the Sanhedrin, the Jewish supreme court, belonged to one of these groups. The Pharisees, the larger and better-liked of the two, obsessively followed the law in an effort to earn righteousness, developing “the oral law as a ‘fence around the Torah,’ which included detailed interpretations, applications, and amplifications of the written Scriptures to enable people to obey them properly.”⁵ They were known for a legalistic approach in their relationship with God. The Sadducees, typically aristocratic landowners, adhered only to the first five books of Scripture. While the two religious groups disagreed on many issues, both believed Jewish heritage ensured their status before God, a false security both John and Jesus exposed.
content.zh-Hant: 施洗約翰應驗了預言：他在曠野呼喊，為彌賽亞預備道路（賽 40:3）。約翰就像王的傳令官，在王前面先行，使道路平坦、方便通行，並向一座城或一個城鎮宣布王即將抵達。經過大約四百年先知沉默的時期，約翰呼召百姓回轉歸向神，就像以利亞在列王紀上第18章所做的一樣。在這段時期，法利賽人和撒都該人就像宗教政治團體；公會這個猶太人的最高法院，大多數成員屬於其中一個團體。法利賽人是兩者中人數較多、也較受人喜愛的一方，他們執著地遵守律法，企圖藉此取得公義，並發展出「口述律法作為『妥拉周圍的籬笆』，其中包括對成文聖經的詳細解釋、應用和擴充，好使人能正確遵守」的做法。⁵ 他們在與神的關係上採取律法主義的方式，這一點廣為人知。撒都該人通常是貴族地主，只承認聖經的前五卷書。這兩個宗教團體雖在許多問題上意見不一，卻都相信猶太人的血統能確保他們在神面前的地位；這種虛假的安全感，約翰和耶穌都揭露了。

content.en: Repentance is a response to God’s gracious call to salvation. It includes a genuine sorrow for one’s sin (Luke 5:1-11), a turning away from one’s sin toward Christ (Acts 26:15-20), and a life that reflects lasting change and transformation (Ps. 119:57-60). This is the human response to God’s salvation, in other words, how we turn to Him and accept what He’s done for us.
content.zh-Hant: 悔改是人對神以恩典發出的救恩呼召所作的回應。悔改包括真誠地為自己的罪憂傷（路 5:1-11）、離開自己的罪轉向基督（徒 26:15-20），以及活出持久改變與更新的生命（詩 119:57-60）。這就是人對神救恩的回應；換句話說，這是我們轉向祂，並接受祂為我們所成就之事的方式。

content.en: God, thank you for offering salvation through your son, not through our efforts or lineage. We can’t boast in our salvation because we did nothing to deserve it. Help us to elevate Jesus in the way we live our lives—to display fruit of repentant hearts.
content.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢藉著祢的兒子賜下救恩，而不是藉著我們的努力或血統。我們不能因自己的救恩自誇，因為我們沒有做任何配得救恩的事。求祢幫助我們在生活中高舉耶穌——顯出悔改的心所結的果子。

question.en: How easily can you tell when something is fake (1=I can’t tell; 10=It’s always obvious)?
question.zh-Hant: 你有多容易分辨某樣東西是假的？（1＝我分辨不出來；10＝總是一目了然）

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:

question.en: If someone gave you the option to hear good news or bad news first, which would you choose? Why?
What have you noticed about news on television? Does it lean more toward bad news or good news?
Why is it helpful to surround ourselves with people who tell us what we need to hear instead of people who tell us what we want to hear?

content.en: If you watch the news on television, you probably notice more bad news than good news. Culture leans toward bad news and thrives on emotional reaction. But when it comes to truth in our personal lives, we lean away from the bad parts. We want to hear only what’s good. Today, our lesson shows that sometimes the hard truth is what we need to hear most.
content.zh-Hant: 如果你在電視上看新聞，你可能會注意到壞消息比好消息多。我們的文化偏向壞消息，也靠激起情緒反應而蓬勃發展。但說到我們個人生活中的真理，我們卻傾向於避開那些不好的部分。我們只想聽好的一面。今天的課程讓我們看見，有時候我們最需要聽的，正是那個艱難的真相。

cultural_connection.en: Do any of us strive to be fake? Do any of us want people to look at us and see a hypocrite, an impostor? Probably not. We want people to see who we really are—to be known. At the same time, we fear being known because people will see the worst parts of us—qualities and insecurities we so desperately try to hide. Want a little hope? Actually, a lot of hope? God knows you (Ps. 139:1). He knows every single part. He has always known you—your failures, your sin, your fears, your questions, your worries, your insecurities, your shame. He doesn’t want you to pretend or to hide any of it from Him. God calls you to bring what He already knows and lay it all down in exchange for abundant, authentic life. How? Confess and repent of your sin, throw off all the things that hinder you (Heb. 12:1), be transparent with the Lord, and walk in the joy of being known by Him.

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We Repent

question.en: What was John’s first word to the crowds? Would his message attract crowds today? What messages attract people now?
question.zh-Hant: **約翰對群眾說的第一句話是什麼？他的信息今天會吸引群眾嗎？現在什麼信息會吸引人？**

answer.en: John’s first word was “repent.” Basically, John told God’s people, the Jews, that they weren’t living like God’s people and that they needed to confess their sins and live in a way that pleased Him. John called them out! Today, this message isn’t attractive; calling people up to God’s standard is often offensive, even in our churches, so we refrain from pointing out sin and the need for repentance. We center our messages on love, acceptance, and forgiveness (all good and true), but if we leave out repentance, then we leave out humanity’s need for a Savior: Jesus.
answer.zh-Hant: 約翰說的第一句話是「你們應當悔改！」基本上，約翰告訴神的子民，也就是猶太人，他們沒有活出神子民的樣式，需要承認自己的罪，並以討祂喜悅的方式生活。約翰當面指出他們的問題！今天，這個信息並不吸引人；呼召人達到神的標準常常令人反感，即使在我們的教會中也是如此，因此我們避免指出罪以及悔改的需要。**我們把信息的中心放在愛、接納和赦免上（這些全都是美好且真實的），但如果我們省略悔改，就等於忽略了人類對救主的需要，而這位救主就是耶穌。**

question.en: Describe John’s lifestyle. Why did he live this way? Should we?
question.zh-Hant: **描述約翰的生活方式。他為什麼這樣生活？我們也應該如此嗎？**

answer.en: John was radically devoted to God and to the message God had given him to share— even if it was offensive. John lived sacrificially, unconcerned with worldly comfort; none of it mattered. He staked his life on the reality that God’s kingdom was supreme—and it was coming. Does God expect all of us to live in the wilderness and survive on bugs and honey? Not likely. But He does call us to live sacrificially, wholly devoted to Him. He calls us to share the gospel boldly, even when it’s offensive to our culture. He calls us to live with eternity in mind instead of striving to make this world our home.

question.en: What is the kingdom of heaven? Where is it? How is it “at hand” (v. 2)?
question.zh-Hant: **天國是什麼？它在哪裡？第2節所說的「近了」是什麼意思？**

answer.en: We hear “kingdom of heaven,” or “kingdom of God,” and think the phrase refers to heaven only, where God dwells on His throne and where believers spend eternity. But the kingdom of heaven exists in a few ways. First, as the King of kings, Jesus ushered His kingdom to earth; His presence here meant God’s kingdom had come in a new way. Jesus was Immanuel, “God with us,” who came near to offer us a place in His kingdom. Next, because Christ now dwells in every believer through the Holy Spirit, God’s kingdom is here, now—the rule and reign of God within us. We are living stones and spiritual houses in God’s kingdom (1 Pet. 2:5). And still in another sense, though the kingdom of heaven has already come through Jesus’s birth and through His Spirit, it is also yet to come—when Jesus will bring His kingdom fully. This kingdom will remain forever, free of sin and pain and death. Jesus will restore all of creation, making all things new, and believers will worship Him forever (Rev. 21:1-5). Because of Jesus’s life, death, resurrection, and ascension to the Father, we get to live as citizens of God’s kingdom here and now! We don’t wait for eternity! Because Jesus came near and offered His life, we are God’s sons and daughters, called to live for His kingdom rather than our worldly kingdoms.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們聽到「天國」或「神的國」，就會想到這個詞語只指天上，也就是神坐在寶座上居住的地方，以及信徒度過永恆的地方。但天國以幾種方式存在。首先，耶穌是萬王之王，祂把祂的國帶到地上；祂在這裏的同在意味著神的國以一種新的方式來到了。耶穌是以馬內利，也就是「神與我們同在」，祂親近我們，為要給我們在祂國中有一席之地。其次，因為基督如今藉著聖靈住在每一位信徒裏面，神的國就在這裏、就在現在——神在我們裏面的統治和掌權。我們是神國中的活石和屬靈的房屋（彼前 2:5）。再者，雖然天國已藉著耶穌的出生和祂的聖靈來到，但它也尚未來到——那時耶穌將使祂的國完全降臨。這國度將永遠長存，不再有罪、痛苦和死亡。耶穌要恢復一切受造之物，使一切都變成新的，信徒也要永遠敬拜祂（啟 21:1-5）。**因著耶穌的生活、受死、復活，以及升到父那裏，我們如今就能以神國子民的身分生活！我們不必等到永恆才開始這樣生活！因為耶穌親近我們並獻上祂的生命，我們是神的兒女，蒙召為祂的國而活，而不是為我們屬世的國度而活。**

title.en: We Elevate Jesus When We’re Authentic

question.en: What is John’s attitude toward the religious leaders? Does it surprise you? Explain.
question.zh-Hant: **約翰對宗教領袖的態度是怎樣的？這讓你感到驚訝嗎？請解釋。**

answer.en: Leaders: Share context about the Pharisees and Sadducees. John didn’t use confusing language or soften his message. He called the religious leaders a “brood of vipers”! John knew they hadn’t come to repent and be baptized; they came to assess and critique him and then report back to the religious court. John called out the religious leaders for their hypocrisy, for claiming to belong to God but living for themselves—for their reputations, their pride, and their personal gain—and for leading others to do the same.
answer.zh-Hant: *帶領者：分享法利賽人和撒都該人的背景。* 約翰沒有使用令人困惑的語言，也沒有淡化他的信息。他稱宗教領袖為「毒蛇的種類」！約翰知道他們不是來悔改和受洗的；他們是來評估並批評他，然後回去向宗教法庭報告。**約翰指出宗教領袖的假冒為善：他們聲稱屬於神，卻為自己而活——為自己的名聲、驕傲和個人利益而活——並且帶領別人也這樣做。**

question.en: What does John mean in verse 8? How can our lives contradict that we follow Jesus? Why has this become “normal” for believers?
question.zh-Hant: **約翰在第8節的意思是什麼？我們的生活如何與我們跟隨耶穌相矛盾？為什麼這對信徒來說已經變得「正常」？**

answer.en: John’s message was simple: If you belong to God, then live like it. How often do we need to hear the same message? How often do our lives contradict the worship songs we sing with our lips? Our words are profane and full of gossip; our actions are selfish, prideful, and unloving; our priorities are worldly. We don’t reflect our King. If we’ve repented—confessed sin and turned from it and toward God—then our lives should display the fruit of the Spirit (Gal. 5:22-23). Instead, we’ve normalized lukewarm faith over authentic faith and labeled holiness and godliness as “radical.” Why? Because we strive to fit into a worldly kingdom—a kingdom in which we’re no longer citizens. The truth is that God wants every part of your life. Is this radical? Sure. Will you be different from the world? Absolutely. You’ll be like your King, reflecting His kingdom.
answer.zh-Hant: 約翰的信息很簡單：如果你屬於神，就要照此生活。我們需要聽見同樣的信息多少次？我們的生活有多少次與我們口中所唱的敬拜詩歌相矛盾？我們的言語褻瀆且充滿閒話；我們的行為自私、驕傲又沒有愛；我們的優先次序屬世。我們沒有反映出我們的君王。若我們已經悔改——承認罪，離開罪並轉向神——那麼我們的生命就應該顯出聖靈的果子（加 5:22-23）。**相反地，我們已把不冷不熱的信心正常化，取代了真實的信心，並把聖潔和敬虔標籤為「激進」。**為什麼？因為我們竭力融入一個屬世的國度——一個我們不再是其中國民的國度。**事實是，神要你生命的每一部分。這很激進嗎？當然。你會與世界不同嗎？絕對會。你會像你的君王一樣，反映祂的國度。**

question.en: What does John say won’t make people right with God (v. 9)? What kinds of things do people point to today to say they’re right with God?
question.zh-Hant: **約翰說什麼不能使人在神面前稱義（第9節）？今天人們會指向哪些事情，來宣稱自己在神面前稱義？**

answer.en: Many Jews relied on their ancestry, basing their security in God’s kingdom on being Abraham’s descendants. Today, people point to their families too, claiming security in someone else’s faith. People claim church attendance or biblical knowledge as proof. They point to good morals as evidence of being right with God. The only way we are saved from sin and secure in God’s kingdom is through surrendering our hearts and enthroning Jesus there, by confessing Christ as Lord and repenting of sin. Jesus is our way to the Father (John 14:6).
answer.zh-Hant: 許多猶太人倚靠自己的血統，以自己身為亞伯拉罕的後裔，作為在神國中得保障的根據。今天，人們也指向自己的家人，聲稱自己在別人的信心中得著安全感。人們把參加教會聚會或聖經知識當作證明。他們把良好的道德當作自己在神面前稱義的證據。**我們從罪中得救、並在神國中得著安全的唯一方式，就是讓我們的心降服，讓耶穌在其中登上寶座；藉著承認基督為主，並悔改離開罪。**耶穌是我們到父那裏去的道路（約 14:6）。

question.en: In what areas of your life have you let it become normal to live like the world? What needs to change so that you live as a citizen of heaven?
question.zh-Hant: **在你生命中的哪些方面，你已經任由自己像世人那樣生活，並視之為常態？你需要作出甚麼改變，才能活得像天上國民？**

answer.en: God wants us to be real and desires for us to follow Him authentically. He isn’t fooled by our efforts at pretending to follow Him. But we live in a culture that specializes in faking it. Think about it: How easily can we fake a perfect life on social media, when in reality, life is falling apart? So, is it really that surprising when this spills over into our walk with God? We’ve gotten good at faking intimacy with the Lord. We’ve normalized living like the world in certain areas of our lives. Maybe you use the same language as unbelievers in your classes. Maybe your priorities look like the world’s priorities, and your time doesn’t reflect that you value God’s Word, prayer, or godly community. Maybe you date like the world dates and justify being in a relationship with someone who brings you down spiritually. Maybe you sometimes lie or sometimes cheat. The world tells us that all of this is normal. But God’s Word calls us up—to a standard of holiness, even if it requires sacrifice, even when it’s not easy. The good news is that Jesus showed us the way.
answer.zh-Hant: 神希望我們真實，也渴望我們真實地跟隨祂。我們*假裝*跟隨祂的努力並不能欺騙祂。但我們活在一個專門製造假象的文化中。想想看：當現實生活正在崩解時，我們卻很容易在社交媒體上假裝擁有完美的生活，不是嗎？所以，當這種情況延伸到我們與神同行的生活中時，真的很令人意外嗎？**我們已經很會假裝與主親密。我們已經把在生命某些方面像世界一樣生活正常化了。**也許你在課堂上使用與未信者相同的語言。也許你的優先次序看起來和世界的優先次序一樣，而你的時間安排沒有反映出你看重神的話語、禱告或敬虔的群體生活。也許你按照世界的方式約會，還為自己和一個在靈性上使你墮落的人交往找藉口。也許你有時說謊，有時作弊。世界告訴我們，這一切都是*正常*的。**但神的話語呼召我們向上，達到聖潔的標準，即使這需要犧牲，即使這並不容易。好消息是，耶穌已經向我們指明了道路。**

content.en:
Today’s passage begins with a quote from Isaiah 40, foretelling John the Baptist’s ministry hundreds of years earlier. John the Baptist clearly understood his role to “prepare the way of the Lord” (v. 4), meaning he was called by God to tell others about Jesus coming to earth and how they needed to prepare their hearts to follow Him. How would they prepare their hearts to follow Jesus? By repentance. Repentance is the act of turning from sin, turning to God, and seeking Him wholeheartedly. As John the Baptist spoke to the people coming to be baptized, he explained that salvation and repentance are an individual’s decision. Every single person must personally surrender his or her life to Jesus and turn from sin in order to be saved.

Repentance absolutely happens in that moment where we surrender our lives to Jesus and receive God’s gift of salvation; that is a one-time decision. Repentance, though, does not stop there! John told the crowd to “bear fruits in keeping with repentance” (v. 8). In other words, he urged them to live in such a way that their actions proved their faith to be real—repenting from sin, obeying God, and living for Him day after day. Those who do not produce good fruit of a real faith will be cut down and burned (John 15:2-6). May we be like the crowds of people, the tax collectors, and the soldiers who asked what they should do in response to this call to repentance (vv. 10-14). And may we also be people who follow the command to obey God and care deeply for others.

question.en: Where in your life do you need to repent? Write out a prayer to God, confessing specific sins you are struggling with, asking God for forgiveness, and turning back to him with your heart and mind.
How can you allow God to produce good fruit this week through serving others and pointing them to Jesus?

prayer.en: God, I want the actions of my life to be consistent with the faith I claim. Help me to live out the daily practice of repentance, where I keep turning from my sin and keep turning back to you.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，我希望自己生命中的行動，與我所宣認的信心一致。求祢幫助我每天實踐悔改，不斷轉離自己的罪，又不斷回轉歸向祢。**

content.en:
If you think about it, our lives are a lot like clay. We are all being shaped by someone or something. The question is: Who or what is shaping you? If you are consistently choosing to walk in sin, then the ways of the world are shaping your life. If you are consistently choosing to repent of sin and turn to God, then you’re allowing God to shape you and produce good fruit in you! Producing fruit consistent with repentance leads to a life of true freedom and godly living. This true freedom invites us to follow the example of Jesus and serve others through love; it calls us away from sin and works of the flesh (Gal. 5:19-21). When we are in Christ, sin does not have the final say in our lives; by God’s power, we can run from sin and run to Him. This is very good news!

Godly living is about loving God and obeying Him. Today’s passage explores the fruit of the Spirit. Notice that “fruit” is singular, not plural. Yes, we read a whole list of things that we want to show up in our lives, but they all make up one fruit of the Spirit. This fruit is the evidence, or result, of God’s work in our lives, and the proof of it is whether or not love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control show up in our lives. Verse 25 explains what we can do for this fruit to grow in our lives: “Keep in step with the Spirit”—step by step, over and over again. Keep walking with the Lord. Keep being transformed. Keep trusting Him to do the work.

question.en: Which fruit of the Spirit stands out as something that you need to grow in? Ask God to help you change.
What is shaping you: God or the world? What habits can you put in place this week to help ensure you’re being shaped by God instead of by the world?

prayer.en: God, only by your power and presence in my life can I live for you instead of for the world. Help me to keep in step with the Spirit and let you be the one who shapes me.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，惟有藉著祢的能力和祢在我生命中的同在，我才能為祢而活，而不是為世界而活。求祢幫助我繼續靠聖靈而行，讓祢成為塑造我的那一位。**

content.en:
Have you ever done less actual cleaning of your room and more shoving your things into the closet (or under your bed or into any spot where you can find space)? Your room might appear cleaner, but the mess is still very much there. Whether or not you can relate to ever fake cleaning your room, we all do something similar with our sins. Instead of confessing our sin, we can sometimes turn to hiding our sins or pretending like they don’t exist. (Humanity has done this from the very beginning, starting with Adam and Eve in Genesis.) Do we ever successfully hide our sins from God? Nope! He sees and knows everything about us, and He wants more for us than frantically hiding our sin. God invites us into a better way—out of hiding our sins from Him and into confessing our sins to Him.

Covering up or hiding sin might feel like the comfortable or safe thing to do in the moment to avoid feelings like guilt, fear, and embarrassment, but this verse reminds us that in the long run, we will never prosper from it. It may feel good at first to cover up our sins, but when we do that, we miss out on God’s forgiveness and true freedom. In fact, according to God’s Word, fear, shame, or duty will never lead us to true repentance; only God’s goodness and kindness actually compel us to run from our sin and instead run to Him (Rom. 2:4). When we confess and repent of our sins, we find God’s rich mercy and total forgiveness. He is patient and faithful to forgive, so let’s run to God and repent!

question.en: What is hard for you about confessing your sins to God instead of trying to hide them?
We are safest when we run to God with our sins and confess everything. Take some time to write out a prayer of confession and repentance, even if it feels uncomfortable.

prayer.en: God, thank you for showing me mercy and for being faithful to forgive. Help me to have the courage to stop trying to hide my sins from you and instead run to you in repentance so that I can find true freedom.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，感謝祢向我施憐憫，並信實地赦免我。求祢幫助我有勇氣，不再試圖向祢隱藏自己的罪，而是帶著悔改奔向祢，使我可以尋見真正的自由。**

content.en:
We pick up in the middle of 2 Corinthians 7 today, but in the first eight verses of the chapter, Paul addressed the letter he previously wrote to the believers in Corinth, urging them to return to God. He explained how he rejoiced when he heard that these believers grieved (yes, you read that right). The grief that Paul celebrated in these believers was what he called “godly grief.” Paul introduced the major difference between godly grief and worldly grief. Godly grief leads to repentance. Repentance is true brokenness over sinning against God—our Father, Creator, and Friend—but is not only a feeling of brokenness. True brokenness or godly grief always leads to the action of turning from our sin and returning to God in repentance. Alternatively, worldly grief leads us into a spiral of shame that we were never meant to experience. Grief must be so much more than just something we feel; it must lead to action and obedience.

Worldly grief keeps you feeling stuck in shame. Godly grief wakes you up to the reality that you are set free from the power of sin because of God’s gift of forgiveness. Worldly grief says, “I am a failure or mistake.” Godly grief says, “I have failed or made a mistake, but I am not defined by my sin. I am loved by God, forgiven, and invited to repent.” Worldly grief may lead to despair and distraction, but godly grief leads to dependence and devotion. Paul pointed out “what earnestness” this godly grief has produced in these believers (v. 11). In other words, godly grief leads believers to quickly and sincerely obey God. Great fruit always comes from godly grief, including love for God, anger towards sin, longing for God’s Word, and passion to obey.

question.en: Where do you see worldly grief show up in your life when it comes to dealing with your own sin?
What would it look like to approach your sin with godly grief and repentance? What needs to change?

prayer.en: God, thank you for your gift of forgiveness and freedom in Jesus. Remind my heart that you call me to godly grief, repentance, and obedience.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，感謝祢在耶穌裏賜下赦免和自由。求祢提醒我的心，祢呼召我要依著祢的意思憂愁、悔改並順服。**

content.en:
We live in a world of constant winners, gold medals, championship rings, and celebrations for “The Best Whatever.” It can be tempting to live with the mindset that we must constantly compete against others, prove our worth, and be better than everyone else. In a world of people trying to become greater, John understood that the gospel of Jesus invites all believers to live differently and become less. To be clear, when John says in verse 11 that he is not worthy to remove his sandals, John is not contradicting the Word of God and saying that his life has no value. Being “less than” and becoming less is hugely different. John knew that he was made by God, loved by God, and chosen by God to come before Jesus to point others to Him. He was even related to Jesus, but he did not let those things lead him to live from a place of pride or false significance. Instead, those things led him to live from a place of humility and worship. John knew he was a messenger of the gospel; he was not the Messiah. John knew he was beloved by God, but not better than or equal to God.

May we adopt the same heart and mindset that John modeled for us—humbling ourselves in order to magnify God alone, making sure God’s work in us is the most important thing about us, and pointing others to Jesus instead of ourselves. This doesn’t mean that we live like we have no value. We have great value! We are made in the image of God and forever loved by Him. But we should let the good news not puff us up in pride but free us up to share His love with everyone we meet.

question.en: How do you relate to the struggle to prove your worth, be recognized by others, or be better than everyone else?
How can you follow the example of John the Baptist and become less so that everyone around you sees more of Jesus in you?

prayer.en: God, thank you for loving me and creating me in your image. Help me find my worth in you alone and fight the temptation to be important in the eyes of other people. I want my life to make much of you and only you.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，感謝祢愛我，並照著祢的形像創造我。求祢幫助我單單在祢裏面尋見自己的價值，並抵擋那想要在別人眼中顯得重要的試探。我渴望自己的生命惟獨高舉祢、尊祢為大。**
